newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - THAI NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - THAI NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- As Thais scramble to hoard goods and withdraw deposits amid a whirlwind of economic rumours, ex-premier Anand Panyarachun calls on the government to resign, saying the public's faith in it has evaporated at a time when confidence in leaders means life or death for the country. In his strongest criticism to date of the besieged government, Anand says Chavalit's only other option is to undertake a major cabinet reshuffle to try to restore confidence. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- In a desperate attempt to stem the repercussions from a severe lack of confidence in the government following two days of depositor jitters, the prime minister enlists the support of the country's four major banks. Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has met representatives of the banks and obtains their agreement to rescue smaller institutions drained by a two-day run on deposits sparked by Tuesday's suspension of 42 finance firms. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- One of Thailand's most controversial murder cases unfolded anew when the Samut Prakan provincial court found three defendants, including a woman dubbed Jao Mae (godmother) of Patpong red-light district, guilty of conspiring to murder Sherry-Ann Duncan 11 years ago and sentenced all three to death. (THE NATION)

- The commerce ministry will keep the average inflation rate for the whole year within 8-9 percent, following implementation of the International Monetary Fund's economic rescue package, says Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee. He says the consumer price index during the first seven months of the year rose only 4.5 percent, compared to the same period last year. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Telephone Organisation of Thailand (TOT) expects to maintain existing telephone rates even though the decision will hurt private concessionaires forced to shoulder higher costs based on the value-added tax hike. TOT President Satien Pitaganun says the issue has been discussed at a board meeting. However, no final decision has been made and the topic will be discussed again on August 13 at a meeting chairs by Transport and Communications permanent secretary. (BANGKOK POST)
